summary: Created from the MPI-424 brainstorm, and it is the card everything else waits on. Toolbar becomes three groups - Mask (brush, detect, adjust, shapes), Paint (brush, shapes), Composite (mask comp, paint comp) - and Detect becomes a COLLAPSE BUTTON that opens a small vertical strip outside the tool panel with points / text / auto, dismissing itself on an unhovered timer. No corner triangle and no long-press: the user rejected both by name. Deliberately NOT in scope, and this is the simplification that keeps the card small: the three detect modes are NOT collapsed into one mode - they stay maskPoints / maskText / maskDetect in TOOL_OPTIONS_REGISTRY and _MASK_TOOLS, and only their presentation moves. The toolbar already renders grouped stacks, so the only new component is the floating strip. This card reverses a decision recorded in MpiHistoryTools.js ('Shapes joins this group; it does not become a switcher') and must update that comment rather than leave it contradicting the code.

Compact plan attached (tasks/MPI-425/plan.md) and the card shrank. Three decisions were settled with the user BEFORE planning so implementation stops for nothing: clicking Detect opens the strip and activates nothing (fixed icon, no last-used identity); Paint will keep the PromptBox and Composite will not, recorded now for MPI-375/MPI-373 without adding dead branches here; and only working tools ship, so this card delivers just the Mask group as brush plus the Detect strip while Adjust/Shapes/Paint/Composite buttons arrive with their own cards. Mechanism found while planning: MpiPopup is already used in this very file for the rail hover tooltip (portals to body, position right, triggerEl), so the strip needs no new positioning code - but both anchor to the same spot on the same button, so the tooltip must be suppressed while the strip is open and the strip must not reuse _tip, which is destroyed on every hover. Verify mode user-ux: the auto-dismiss constant will be wrong on the first guess and the user has to feel it.
